title.narrative: Garanti SME stöd till Equity BCDC
Guarantee SME support to Equity BCDC

description.narrative:
Insatsen är en låneportföljgaranti från Sida och USAID/DFC som syftar till att främja tillgången till finansiering för mikroföretag och små och medelstora företag (MSME) i Demokratiska Republiken Kongo, med fokus på jordbrukssektorn och sektorn för förnybar energi, som bidrar till landets ekonomiska tillväxt.
Insatsen faller under Strategin för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete med Demokratiska republiken Kongo, 2021-2025. De stödområden som är relevanta för insatsen är miljö, hållbart utnyttjande av naturresurser och livsmedelstrygghet.

This contribution is a Sida and USAID/DFC loan portfolio guarantee intended to promote access to finance for Micro Small and Medium sized enterprises (MSME) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with focus on the agriculture and renewable energy sector contributing to the economic growth of the country.
The intervention falls under the Strategy for Sweden’s development cooperation with Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2021-2025. The support areas relevant for this contribution are environment, sustainable use of natural resources, and food security.

The new proposed guarantee contribution to Equity BCDC is based on the experiences from the first guarantee, which has been successful in terms of utilization and in demonstrating additionality and increasing the access to finance for MSMEs, not at least within the agricultural sector. The market demand from businesses for financing is large and unmet in the financial market as of today, which was a main reason for DFC and Sida to in a joint effort launch a process of call for expression of interest to assess the conditions for implementing a new guarantee facility in DRC. DFC and Sida based this selection process on a predetermined selection criteria and assessed all of the financial institutions applying for the guarantee, of which Equity BCDC was determined to be the most suitable institution for a guarantee collaboration.
The new guarantee will focus on enabling Equity BCDC to extend their lending to MSMEs, cooperatives, businesses within agriculture, investments in renewable energy as well as having a clear target of including women run and/or owned businesses in DRC (40 % of the total guaranteed portfolio will be allocated to this target group).

The level of banking access remains low in the Democratic Republic of Congo, at approximately 6%. This is why it is necessary to support entrepreneurs with little or no collateral, those with fragile businesses, or those whose activities are not supported by financial and banking institutions.
Regarding Equity BCDC, significant organizational changes were observed at various management levels within the bank in November 2024, including that of the Managing Director. There was also an injection of approximately €70 million from Equity Group Holdings. Willy Mulamba was appointed as the new Managing Director, taking over from Celestin Mukeba, who has led the bank since 2020. The new CEO has proven expertise in the field and extensive experience in the financial services sector, having previously headed one of the DRC's leading banks: City Bank RDC. He previously served as President of the Congolese Banking Association of the DRC. This appointment comes at a time when EquityBCDC is experiencing significant expansion. The bank saw its client base grow by 50% in 2022, from 1.2 million to 1.7 million. The outgoing CEO announced the goal of reaching 5 million new clients by 2025 and reaching around 30 million clients by 2030.
Regarding the use of the guarantee for fiscal year 2024, the second year, the Bank was able to grant approximately 31 loans to micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises, as well as agricultural cooperatives. This essentially brings the total loans granted to USD 3,186,996 as of December 31, 2024 (Source: DFC CMS). This represents 15% of the total guarantee amount, or USD 20 million. The average loan is estimated at approximately USD 99,594. The lowest loan amount is estimated at USD 4,000 and the highest at USD 200,000. This indicates that micro and small businesses are included.
In terms of intervention sectors and target audience, 32% of loans were allocated to agricultural cooperatives and MSMEs, 23% to trade, 19% to women microenterprise owners across all sectors, 10% to services, and 3% to social sectors. This data shows that the Bank is increasingly providing financing to the agricultural sector. To determine whether pure agriculture benefits from financial support from the Bank, it will be essential to understand the specifics of this financing during upcoming field missions.
For Sweden, the use of the guarantee is considered satisfactory. This is a good start. The bank has managed to raise a significant amount to grant loans according to the eligibility criteria and agreed priority sectors. However, the renewable energy sector was not financed. We hope this situation will improve in 2025, as the bank has benefited from assistance from USAID and Sida. This particularly concerns the training offered by USAID and Sida to bank employees in October 2024, which was attended by more than 50 agents: on-site in Kinshasa and online for other cities (Goma, Bukavu, Bas Congo, Katanga, etc.).
In addition to the training, other actions have been implemented to help the Bank better understand the terms of the Agreement to enable them to better utilize the guarantor. These include interviews with the Bank's CEO, the Equity Foundation, and all agents involved in credit, reporting, and sales.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
